subject: Re: Follow-up: Acme pricing & context-length profiling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Acme pricing & context-length profiling

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the chat today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can run a pricing/unit-econ exercise: 

- Use cases: multi-doc summarization + Q&A pipeline, weekly batch extraction, and an incident-response assistant.
- Monthly token estimate you mentioned: ~150M tokens/mo (combined prompts + completions).
- Context needs: majority are short (<=8k), but ~10% of jobs need longer context (32k); a handful (edge cases) may want 128k for legal bundles.
- Avg sizes (need confirmation): prompt ~200-400 tokens, completion ~800-1,200 tokens for summaries (batch jobs shorter).
- Target budget: you mentioned a range but not a hard $/1M target — if you can call that out, we can map scenarios.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you’re ok, send a small sample of anonymized logs (or a small ndjson of prompts + completion lengths) so we can profile exact distribution.
2) I’ll share a preliminary pricing estimate (per-1M token unit economics at 8k/32k/128k SKUs) and a short sensitivity table showing cost at 100M/150M/300M tokens.
3) Rishi (cc’d) can join a short technical session to go over the memory/latency tradeoffs for 32k vs 8k.

I attached a blank template for the token sample and will follow with a pricing workbook after I get rough confirmation on avg prompt/completion sizes and the % of traffic that actually needs >8k.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0112

Attachments: acme_token_profile_sample.ndjson (template)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Acme pricing & context-length profiling

Hi Marissa —

Great recap — thanks. A few clarifications from our side:

- Monthly tokens: total ~150M tokens/month (this is current pilot; if production rolls out expect 2-3x in 9-12 months).
- Average sizes: prompts ~250 tokens (most are short prompts combined with doc pointers), completions ~900 tokens for the summary flows; extraction jobs are shorter (~150 tokens).
- Context length distribution: ~85% of queries are satisfied within 8k, ~10% will need 32k (long reports consolidated), ~5% are occasional legal bundles that could hit 128k.
- SLA/latency: most interactive flows need sub-1s generation latency (we can accept slightly higher for long-context batch jobs).
- Budget: current pilot budget is $10k- $30k/mo; for a committed production contract we would target unit economics around $1,800 per 1M tokens (open to discussion).

I’ll attach a small sample of anonymized prompts/completion lengths - can you run profiling against that and return the estimated monthly cost at the three SKUs (8k/32k/128k)? Also include the expected latency tradeoffs and any recommended caching/batching levers.

Thanks —
Sam
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corporation
sam.patel@acme.com

Attachments: acme_token_profile_sample.ndjson

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Acme pricing & context-length profiling

Sam —

Appreciate the detail, that’s exactly what we need. Quick notes on approach and what I’ll send by EOD Monday: 

- Profiling: we’ll ingest the sample and compute distribution (prompt/completion token histograms) and produce per-SKU cost estimates factoring in batching/caching assumptions.
- Assumptions I’ll use (and can adjust based on feedback): 20% batching gain on average for completions, prefix caching for repeated docs (saves ~15% token count on average), and differentiated CPU/GPU routing for <8k vs >8k to control $/token.
- Unit pricing scenarios: I’ll model three rate cards: (A) 8k SKU, (B) 32k SKU (small premium), (C) 128k SKU (higher premium). Each will show $/1M token and total month cost for 100M/150M/300M token tiers.

Can you confirm you’re comfortable with us using the anonymized sample for profiling (and that it contains no PII)? If yes, I’ll run the analysis and send the workbook (redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx).

Also, can we schedule a 30-min SE session next Wed to walk Rishi through the more technical tradeoffs?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx (will be sent after profiling)

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 14:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Acme pricing & context-length profiling

Marissa / Sam —

We’re good to proceed. I’ve attached the anonymized token-length sample (ndjson) and the procurement team cleared sharing for profiling - no PII in the sample. Please run the profiling and share the workbook.

A couple procurement notes:
- We prefer multi-tier pricing with clear overage rules.
- For an initial 12-month committed contract we can discuss a blended $/1M token figure; initial target remains ~$1,800 per 1M tokens.

Next steps: run profiling, return cost scenarios, then we’ll route to procurement for commercial discussion.

Olivia Chen
Head of Business Ops, Acme Corporation

Attachments: acme_token_profile_sample.ndjson

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Acme pricing & context-length profiling

Thanks team —

I’ll take the sample and run the token distribution + latency sensitivity tests tomorrow. High-level guidance for the workbook I’ll include:
- 8k SKU: lowest $/1M token; good for ~85% of traffic; expect best latency and throughput.
- 32k SKU: modest premium (we’ll show X% price increase) - recommended for the 10% of flows you mentioned. We’ll include a canary strategy (route only long-doc requests to 32k pool to limit cost).
- 128k SKU: significant premium and lower throughput; keep for legal bundles - consider pre-processing to chunk and re-rank to reduce effective context needs.

I’ll include a sample sensitivity table that maps target $/1M tokens (you listed $1,800) to monthly spend at your 150M baseline and the 2x/3x scale scenarios.

Marissa - I’m available Jun 30 or Jul 1 for the SE session; pick 30 mins and I’ll block it.

- Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
